flashcard_questions.q: Which metal ion gives a crimson flame in a flame test?
Which metal ion gives a yellow flame in a flame test?
Which metal ion gives a lilac flame in a flame test?
Which metal ion gives an orange-red flame in a flame test?
Which metal ion gives a green flame in a flame test?
Why is the nichrome wire cleaned with hydrochloric acid between flame tests?
flashcard_questions.a: To avoid contamination from the previous sample.

flashcard_questions.q: Which metal ion gives a blue precipitate with sodium hydroxide solution?
Which metal ion gives a green precipitate with sodium hydroxide solution?
Which metal ion gives a brown precipitate with sodium hydroxide solution?
Which white hydroxide precipitate dissolves when excess sodium hydroxide is added?
Which gas is given off when dilute acid is added to a carbonate?
With silver nitrate, chloride gives a ____ precipitate, bromide ____ and iodide ____.
Why is dilute nitric acid added before silver nitrate in the halide test?
flashcard_questions.a: To remove carbonate or sulfite ions that would give false positives.

flashcard_questions.q: Which reagent is added after dilute hydrochloric acid to test for sulfate ions?
How does flame emission spectroscopy identify a metal ion?
flashcard_questions.a: Each element emits a unique line spectrum of wavelengths.

notes: 15 cards: 5 colour→ion flame test cards and 4 colour→ion hydroxide precipitate cards, all written colour-first so no two cards share an answer, 1 halide cloze covering the three silver halide colours in one card (the FLASHCARD_RULES multi-blank cloze pattern), 3 practical-reasoning cards (wire cleaning, nitric acid first, barium chloride reagent), 1 gas identification, 1 instrumental method card. Dropped the instrumental method advantage/disadvantage lists as enumerations, and the cation/anion definitions as low-yield.
